answer: Complete. `analysis.py` (self-contained, numpy+math only, 149 lines) implements a horizon-indexed, model-free optimistic Q-learning agent with windowed empirical-Bernstein optimism and mean-only target propagation, tuned once as a single shared configuration on the public calibration suite using fresh independent seeds (never the 3 paired eval seeds, which I showed carry ±5–9 per-case seed noise). Final configuration: (1) horizon-indexed Q via O(H*S*A) scalar tables N/M/V2 only — no transition model, no next-state counts, no next-state enumeration, no replay, no posterior sampling, no episode trace; (2) targets use mean-only child values max_a M[h+1,s',a'] so confidence bonuses never enter targets (bounding target drift); (3) bounded-memory (windowed) online updates of target mean and second moment with W = clip(5*S*A, 30, 120) — stale samples collected while downstream Q was immature are forgotten, removing the drift burn-in without H*S*A*S storage; (4) explicit optimism via bonus b = 1.0*sqrt(2*v̂*L/n_eff) + 0.1*b_rem*L/(n−1) with n_eff = min(n,W), v̂ = windowed empirical target variance (degrades gracefully if rewards/continuations are stochastic), L = log(3*S*A*H*K), optimistic initialization (H−h+1)*rmax for unvisited cells; (5) all Q values clipped to the valid remaining-horizon range, act/observe exception-free, actions plain ints. Mechanism selection: pinned/batched updates were dropped (buffered commits would depart from per-visit online updates); the two-timescale slow-target variant gave no measurable benefit over windowed statistics and was also dropped. Evidence: official eval-seed run total regret 148.93 vs published plain UCB-B 207.99 and strong reference 77.57 (per case: noisy_fork 12.30 vs 26.34, variance_cascade 11.04 vs 10.24, stable_volatile 26.30 vs 32.75); on two independent 24-seed fresh batches the submission totals 49.95/50.63 mean-regret vs UCB-B 105.66 (0.48×) with a balanced per-case profile 15.9–18.1 on every case in both batches; on six synthetic hidden-dimension MDPs (S 4–8, A 2–3, H 12–16, K 480–750, sparse/dense kernels) it scores 0.30–0.65× UCB-B (mean 0.49×) and beats a do-nothing agent everywhere; zero invalid actions/errors; 0.5 s for the largest hidden-size case. Public example MDP runs cleanly through the official runner (0 invalid, 0 errors).

final_configuration.algorithm: horizon-indexed optimistic Q-learning, model-free, per-visit online updates
final_configuration.storage: O(H*S*A) scalars (N, M, V2); no episode trace needed
final_configuration.target_rule: mean-only child value max_a M[h+1,s',a']; bonuses never enter targets
final_configuration.drift_mechanism: bounded-memory windowed online updates (W = clip(5*S*A, 30, 120)) for target mean and second moment = version-stamped forgetting realized as bounded-memory statistics
final_configuration.bonus: 1.0*sqrt(2*vhat*L/min(n,W)) + 0.1*b_rem*L/(n-1), L = log(3*S*A*H*K), vhat = windowed empirical variance of sampled targets
final_configuration.selection: greedy on M + bonus; optimistic init (H-h+1)*rmax for unvisited cells; all values clipped to remaining-horizon range
final_configuration.rejected_variants: pinned/batched updates (constraint), two-timescale slow targets (no benefit), Hoeffding-only, maxgap, growing windows, floor decay, annealed/ETE schedules (within-noise gains, added K-sensitivity)
